You're doing a deep research pass on Plutonium (the CoD private-server framework) and building customer-facing documentation for Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting platform, staging tree /opt/nxeon-staging — work ONLY in staging, never /opt/nxeon prod. Never run `npm run build`; verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`).

IMPORTANT — avoid file conflicts: a SEPARATE agent is currently building/editing the Plutonium landing pages (`app/(marketing)/plutonium-t4-hosting/page.tsx`, `-t5-`, `-t6-`, `-iw5-hosting`) and the shared game-catalog files (`lib/games.ts`, `lib/game-control.ts`, etc.) right now. Do NOT edit any of those files. Your job is to (a) do deep research, and (b) build NEW, separate documentation pages that don't exist yet. If you need to reference something about pricing/family keys from the landing pages, only READ them, don't edit.

Same safety framing as the rest of the Plutonium work today — re-read and follow: brand everything as "Plutonium T4/T5/T6/IW5 hosting" or "WaW/BO1/BO2/MW3", NEVER "Call of Duty hosting" anywhere. No official Activision/CoD imagery. Grep your own output for "call of duty"/"activision" (case-insensitive) before finishing, zero hits outside a deliberate non-affiliation disclaimer if used.

## Research phase

The owner linked `https://plutonium.pw/docs/` as a source, but it returns HTTP 403 to direct fetches (bot protection). Work around this:
1. Try `https://web.archive.org/web/2026*/https://plutonium.pw/docs/` and related archived snapshots of `plutonium.pw/docs/dedicated-servers/`, `plutonium.pw/docs/server/t4/`, `/t5/`, `/t6/`, and `plutonium.pw/docs/install/` — the Wayback Machine often isn't behind the same bot-protection and may have full page content and even images archived.
2. Cross-reference via WebSearch and WebFetch against third-party sources that mirror/paraphrase the same official instructions: hosting company docs (Legion Hosting, HGMServers, CB Servers — `docs.cbservers.xyz/games/t5` was found earlier), community forum guides (`forum.plutonium.pw` threads), and YouTube-guide descriptions/transcripts if searchable.
3. Specifically extract, for EACH of the 4 titles (T4/WaW, T5/BO1, T6/BO2, IW5/MW3):
   - **How a PLAYER connects to a server** (not the server owner) — do they need the Plutonium launcher installed client-side? Do they need their own legal copy of the base game? Is there an in-game server browser, or do they connect via a direct IP/command? This is critical customer-education content — many people will not know they need the Plutonium client themselves before they can even attempt to join, and will think something's broken with the server.
   - **Prerequisites** a customer needs before ordering: own the base game legally, have Plutonium client installed, a `plutonium.pw` account (needed for T6's SERVER_KEY specifically, confirm if the others need an account too or work differently).
   - **Realistic setup process honesty check**: is it truly one-click/plug-and-play once ordered, or are there real manual steps (uploading game files via SFTP for T4/T5, generating a SERVER_KEY for T6, Steam Tool setup for IW5)? Get this right per-title — don't oversell any of them as "instant" if they're not.
   - **Modding**: what's the real modding scene for each title on Plutonium — custom maps, zombies mods, custom killstreaks/scripts, mod menus, whatever is genuinely common and documented in the community. Note which titles have an active modding scene vs. thin/none.
   - **Any real screenshots** you can find (via Wayback Machine or elsewhere) showing the actual connect flow, launcher UI, or server setup — if found, note the source URL; if you can download one legitimately (a Wayback-archived image, or a screenshot embedded in a public GitHub README/wiki), save it, but do NOT fabricate a "screenshot" or misrepresent unrelated art as a screenshot.

## Build phase

Create a documentation section for Plutonium hosting — check how existing docs content is structured in this codebase first (search for `/docs` route, `app/docs/` or similar, and check `/admin/docs` mentioned in project conventions — read a couple of existing doc pages to match the established pattern/component structure exactly, don't invent a new docs system).

Build a clear, honest, well-organized doc page (or a few, your judgment — could be one page with a title per section, or 4 sub-pages) covering:
1. "Before you order" — the ownership/legal prerequisites (mirroring the landing pages' safety framing, but here as genuinely useful buyer-education content, not just a liability disclaimer).
2. "How players connect" — per title, the real connection flow including needing the Plutonium client, explained clearly for someone who's never done this before.
3. "Setting up your server" — realistic, honest, per-title setup expectations (what's automated vs. what requires the customer to do something, e.g. upload game files or generate a key).
4. "Modding" — per-title overview of what's realistically possible.
Include real screenshots where you found legitimate ones (with proper local hosting under `public/`, not hotlinking).

Also flag clearly (don't build yet) whether the existing 4 landing pages need updating to reference this new doc page and to correct any "plug and play"-style oversimplification you find in their current copy — read them (don't edit) and report specific line-level suggestions for the other agent/a follow-up pass to apply.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Report back (under 600 words): per-title connection/prerequisite/setup/modding findings (table format), what documentation you built and where, any real screenshots sourced (with provenance), and specific corrections needed on the 4 landing pages (list them precisely, file + what's wrong, for a follow-up task to apply — do not edit those files yourself).

## Installing the Plutonium Launcher

Go to the official Plutonium website at https://plutonium.pw/ and navigate to the "Downloads" section to download plutonium.exe.
